source.author: ov
source.text: Ille etiam picta redimitus tempora mitra, innitens baculo, positis per tempora canis, assimulavit anum cultosque intravit in hortos pomaque mirata est tanto que potentior! inquit, paucaque laudatae dedit oscula, qualia numquam vera dedisset anus, glaebaque incurva resedit suspiciens pandos autumni pondere ramos.
source.text_original: Ille etiam picta redimitus tempora mitra, / innitens baculo, positis per tempora canis, / assimulavit anum cultosque intravit in hortos / pomaque mirata est 'tanto' que 'potentior!' inquit, / paucaque laudatae dedit oscula, qualia numquam / vera dedisset anus, glaebaque incurva resedit / suspiciens pandos autumni pondere ramos.
source.text_english: He too, with his temples bound in a painted mitre, leaning on a staff, with his gray hair arranged about his temples, imitated an old woman and entered the tended gardens, and she, wondering at the apples, exclaimed, So much the more powerful! and gave a few kisses to what she praised—kisses such as no real old woman would ever have given—and she sat down again on a curving clod, looking up at the spreading branches burdened with the weight of autumn.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Thracius hie noctem dulci testudine vates extrahit, ut steterit redimitus tempora vittis Phrixus et iniustas contectus nubibus aras fugerit Inoo linquens Athamanta Learcho; aureus ut iuvenem miserantibus intulit undis vector et astrictis ut sedit cornibus Helle.
reuse.text_original: Thracius hie noctem dulci testudine vates / extrahit, ut steterit redimitus tempora vittis / Phrixus et iniustas contectus nubibus aras / fugerit Inoo linquens Athamanta Learcho; / aureus ut iuvenem miserantibus intulit undis / vector et astrictis ut sedit cornibus Helle.
reuse.text_english: Here the Thracian singer passes the night with his sweet lyre, as Phrixus stood with his temples bound with fillets and, covered by the clouds, fled the unjust altars, leaving Athamas and Learcho for Ino; as the golden one bore the youth on the pitying waves, and as Helle sat upon the clasped horns.
